findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is unstable across processes
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 27 the cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different web workers compute different keys for the same projects and never share cache entries, defeating the optimization. hash() can also be negative and can collide, causing two different project sets to share an eligibility entry and return upsampled counts for non-allowlisted projects or vice versa. Use a deterministic encoding such as comma-joined sorted ids or hashlib.

findings.title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns wrong counts after config change
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 38 allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds. If the project allowlist option changes, queries for up to 60s will use the stale boolean and either apply sum(sample_weight) to non-allowlisted projects (10x inflation) or use raw count() for allowlisted projects (10x undercount). The helper invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation path. Either remove the cache (options.get is already cheap/cached) or wire invalidation/versioning.

findings.title: upsampled_count sum(sample_weight) without null handling undercounts
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1046 upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). Events that were not client-sampled or predate the column have NULL/missing sample_weight and contribute 0/NULL to sum instead of 1, so mixing sampled and unsampled events undercounts. toInt64 on NULL/errors and truncation of fractional weights also corrupts results. It needs coalesce/ifNull handling e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight,1)) with rounding, not a bare sum.

findings.title: Error-query check only matches event.type:error substring
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 137 _is_error_focused_query returns True only if 'event.type:error' is a substring of request query. The common Discover error filter '!event.type:transaction' (used in the same endpoint for dashboard split) is therefore never recognized, so Discover error queries silently skip upsampling and undercount 10x. Conversely a query like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' contains the substring and would incorrectly upsample transaction rows, inflating counts.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 220 _get_event_stats checks is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with the outer closure variable dataset instead of its scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with different datasets (discover vs metrics/transactions) but the upsampling decision stays tied to the original dataset, so split error queries can be incorrectly skipped or applied.

findings.title: Split error query string never seen by upsampling check
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 383 the dashboard-split path builds errors_only_query and transactions_only_query as local strings, but _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET['query'], not the query argument passed to _get_event_stats. The appended 'AND !event.type:transaction' / 'AND event.type:transaction' therefore never affects the upsampling decision, so split Discover error queries are misclassified even if substring handling is fixed.

findings.title: upsampled_count exposed as public function bypasses allowlist
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041 upsampled_count is registered without private=True, unlike the neighboring internal SnQLFunction. Any user can explicitly query upsampled_count() even for projects not in the error-upsampling allowlist, getting 10x-inflated numbers or errors when sample_weight is missing, bypassing the server-side allowlist gate in error_upsampling.py.

findings.title: Only exact count() is rewritten, other aggregates silently stay raw
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 92 transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only columns where lower().strip() == 'count()'. Dashboards/widgets using count_if, count_unique, failure_count, equations, or count() with different aliasing/casing variations keep raw counts while count() buckets are multiplied by sample weight, producing internally inconsistent charts with mixed raw and upsampled series.

findings.title: Integration tests share upsampling cache across mocked allowlists
findings.body: In tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py at line 3552 the OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest cases mock options.get with different allowlists but use the same organization and project ids and never clear the cache in error_upsampling.py. The first test's cached eligibility (60s TTL) leaks into later tests with partial/empty allowlists, making the suite order-dependent and able to falsely pass/fail. Tests must clear the cache key or patch the cache.
